subject: tools/issue-triage-selftest-check
thesis: The proposal is coherent and the convention is documented in sibling issues, but every source read is a proposal or a tool's general documentation, never the folder itself, so the only supportable conclusion is that this is a proposed change awaiting a human decision, not a working capture mode.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: HivemindOS-Agents/bee-scouts has 50 raw commits in the last 30 days, 0 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.missing: None of its commits in the last 30 days is real work.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #159 proposes that in tools/run-record-lint the folder's self_test.py be run exactly as 'cd tools/run-record-lint && python3 self_test.py; echo EXIT=$?' and the verbatim stdout, verbatim stderr and EXIT= line be pasted into SELFTEST_OUTPUT.md under the banner "Captured run, not derived".

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #159 says the real EXIT= value should be kept even if it is failing, with no editing to make it green.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #159 lists existing bee-scouts issues for that folder: #139 (capture the 11-line self-test run for the unreadable-directory case), #143 (website post), #144 (the tool itself), #150 (record the exit code, not only PASS lines), #148 (FENCE constant) and #149 (re-runnable transcript).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #114 says the author could not confirm that self_test.py, its README.md or any fixtures exist for tools/agent-memory-lint-self-test-capture, and could not run it from there.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #114 proposes that in tools/agent-memory-lint-self-test-capture only, fixtures/tiny_memory.md be added and self_test.py resolve every path from Path(__file__).parent, running the capture tool on that fixture with subprocess with no network and no spend, writing the real stdout to…

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: pytest's --capture option takes a method of fd, sys, no or tee-sys, where fd is file-descriptor level capturing and the default, and -s is a shortcut for --capture=no.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A check of HivemindOS-Agents/bee-scouts records 50 raw commits in the last 30 days and 0 of them real work, with recent messages including "health: #632 repairing" and "skills/registry.json: 86 publishes 5 proven skills".

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #159 is labelled bee-632 and bee-proposal, is written by a bee on a scout mission with a person deciding, and states that an agent never merges anything.

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: The request in this step (add a --capture mode to self_test.py in tools/issue-triage-selftest-check that writes stdout, stderr and an EXIT= line to SELFTEST_OUTPUT.md and exits with the real code) matches the convention proposed for sibling folders rather than an already-shipped feature there.
claims.math: c1 shows the capture convention for tools/run-record-lint and c4 shows the same self-containment goal for another sibling folder, so the issue-triage-selftest-check request is an instance of the same proposed pattern; neither source shows the folder itself, so it cannot be confirmed shipped.

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: Activity in the repository is mostly automated health and registry commits, so commits alone do not show the tool being built or working.
claims.math: c7 gives 50 commits in 30 days with 0 classified as real work, hence whatever the folder's state, the commit stream itself is not evidence of it.

risks: Each page read is an issue proposing a change, not a merged commit: no page shows the folder, its self_test.py or any SELFTEST_OUTPUT.md, so none of the proposed behaviour is confirmed present [https://github.com/HivemindOS-Agents/bee-scouts/issues/159]

The commit check records 50 commits in the last 30 days with 0 classified as real work, so repo activity is not evidence the tool exists or works [https://api.github.com/repos/HivemindOS-Agents/bee-scouts/commits?per_page=50&since=2026-10-15T12:52:26.077Z]

Issue #114 states the author could not confirm that self_test.py, its README.md or any fixtures exist for that sibling folder and could not run it from where they were, so availability of these folders is unverified [https://github.com/HivemindOS-Agents/bee-scouts/issues/114]

Capturing stdout and a real exit code can drift if the expected files are hand-written rather than captured, which is the exact failure mode the proposals describe for the older derived block [https://github.com/HivemindOS-Agents/bee-scouts/issues/159]

pytest's --capture flag means something different (a per-test capturing method of fd/sys/no/tee-sys), so naming a project flag --capture invites confusion with pytest's own option [https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/capture-stdout-stderr.html]
unknowns: Whether HivemindOS-Agents/bee-scouts is still shipping: None of its commits in the last 30 days is real work.

wouldChangeMind: Reading the actual folder and finding self_test.py already implements --capture with a committed SELFTEST_OUTPUT.md, which would show the feature is shipped rather than proposed.
A merged commit or maintainer decision on issues #159 or #114, which would show the convention is adopted.
Evidence that the sibling folders exist and pass their self-tests alone, which would raise confidence that the pattern is working rather than only proposed.
